narrative.overview:
The page is a white room with good light. Nothing is decorated: the furniture and the fitted rooms are photographed properly and then given space, and every other element on the page steps back so the photograph reads first. Text is near-black on white, rules are hairlines, headings sit in the normal weight range (500), and exactly one colour — a considered forest green — appears, only where something can be acted on or is live. This is the Nordic-retail craft standard executed straight, with no irony and no smuggled quirk.

Density is low and deliberate. Sections are separated by large vertical gaps (5rem rising to 7rem), headings are followed by air rather than ornament, and a single quiet sand band (#f6f5f2) is the only alternative ground — used to mark the interiors territory, never to add texture. Photography carries the weight; typography carries the facts.

The world has one authored moment: a lead photograph settling into its frame (animate-settle, 0.7s, a 2.5% scale release). Everything else moves only as a response to the pointer — a slow 900ms image scale on hover, an underline, a background tint. A previous canary-yellow stationery world was rejected outright by the user; nothing from it belongs here, and bright yellow, stamp red, monospace chrome and zero-radius card frames are out of the system.
keyCharacteristics: White ground throughout; paper and cream are both pure white by design.
One accent (#2d4a3e), for action and live state only.
Hairline rules (#e6e4de / #d8d5cd); the grid is suggested, never drawn.
One typeface, Hanken Grotesk, at normal weights; headings 500.
A single 4px corner radius, 2px only on icon buttons and focus rings.
No kickers, no eyebrows, no decorative colour, no shadow as decoration.

rules.name: The One Colour Rule
rules.body: accent is the only hue on the page. It is reserved for action and live state; nothing else is coloured. If a surface is green for emphasis rather than for action, the green is wrong.

rules.name: The Free-Path Rule
rules.body: The free action is tinted green; the paid action is near-black. That asymmetry is load-bearing — it tells the visitor which door costs nothing. Do not equalise the two buttons.

rules.name: The Legacy Alias Rule
rules.body: tan, tan-2, tan-soft, bronze, canary and stamp are aliases pointing into this palette so untouched routes move with the world. They are migration plumbing, not tokens. New work names accent, ink, sand.

rules.name: The Normal-Weight Rule
rules.body: Headings are 500. Nothing on a storefront surface goes heavier than 600, and nothing is set in uppercase except label-xs. Weight is not how this system creates emphasis — space and photography are.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: Absolute: no kicker, eyebrow, or small uppercase line above a heading, anywhere. label-xs is chrome for column headings, nav group labels and table headers; if it is sitting above an H1/H2/H3, it is a defect.

rules.name: The Sequence-Only Numbering Rule
rules.body: Section numbers appear in exactly one place — the four fit-out stages (01-04) — because the order of those stages is the information. Numbers are never added to sections for rhythm.

rules.name: The Flat-Page Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the page surface casts a shadow. Shadow is reserved for elements that overlay the page (nav panel, and nothing else today). Scrims (ink/30-ink/40) carry the depth for drawers and sheets instead.

dos: Do keep the ground white (#ffffff) and use sand (#f6f5f2) for at most one alternating band per page.
Do reserve accent (#2d4a3e) for action and live state, and tint the free path green while the paid path stays near-black.
Do let the photograph be the loudest element: fixed aspect ratio, 4px clip, sand placeholder, and type that stays at 500 or lighter beside it.
Do use one radius (4px), with 2px only on icon buttons and focus rings.
Do set counts, prices and dimensions with figure-num so columns of numerals line up.
Do use label-xs for column headings, nav group labels and table headers only.
Do number a sequence only when the order is the information (the four fit-out stages).
Do keep the two trades co-equal in every navigation, grid and footer position.
Do gate "our work" surfaces on DesignImage.origin = OWN_WORK; heroRank ranks composition, not provenance, and several hero-ranked products are supplier catalogue renders.
Do keep motion as a response to the pointer, with one authored exception: animate-settle on a lead photograph.
donts: Don't put a kicker or eyebrow above a heading, anywhere, in any form.
Don't introduce a second hue. Status colours are signals, not palette.
Don't set storefront headings above 600, in uppercase, or in a second typeface.
Don't add shadows to cards, buttons, inputs or bands; shadow belongs only to surfaces overlaying the page.
Don't use 2px borders or zero-radius frames; the stroke is a 1px hairline and the corner is 4px.
Don't name legacy aliases (tan, canary, stamp, bronze) in new work.
Don't apply animate-settle to text — it is scoped to media.
Don't let a product render reach a surface that claims the work is ours.
